The case was originally filed seven years ago by Gambia, a predominantly Muslim nation. Judges on the 15-member panel concluded that Myanmar's military executed mass killings of men and boys, subjected women to widespread rape, and systematically burned or razed hundreds of villages in Northern Rakhine State. The court determined that the only reasonable inference for these coordinated actions was an intentional effort to destroy a substantial part of the Rohingya population, driving at least 700,000 people to flee the Buddhist-majority country.

Because the ruling by the International Court of Justice is final and cannot be appealed, it carries significant legal weight and is expected to influence other international cases, such as South Africa's 2023 accusation of genocide against Israel in Gaza. Both Myanmar and Israel have consistently denied allegations of genocide, arguing their forces were responding legitimately to armed attacks. Myanmar's government specifically utilized hate speech targeting the Rohingya population prior to and during the military offensives.

As a consequence of the ruling, the court mandated that Myanmar provide compensation to the Rohingya for the violations committed, with the exact figures to be determined at a later date. Furthermore, the state is required to facilitate the safe and dignified return of displaced Rohingya to their places of residence and ensure family reunifications. Prior to this landmark decision, international courts had only officially recognized genocide in the 1994 Rwandan genocide, the 1995 Srebrenica killings in Bosnia, and atrocities committed by the Khmer Rouge in Cambodia during the late 1970s.

stories.title: Rabia Ahsan's Husband to Walk Free After Family Files Affidavits
stories.summary:
The homicide case surrounding television anchorperson Rabia Ahsan took a major turn on Thursday when her mother, brother, and sister appeared before a Rawalpindi court to submit affidavits forgiving the prime suspect. The family members declared that the fatal shooting was an accidental incident and stated they had no objection to the release of Ahsan Tahir on bail.

Additional District and Sessions Judge Khurram Saleem approved the post-arrest bail for Tahir against property surety bonds worth Rs200,000, though personal surety bonds submitted earlier were rejected. Tahir's bail was also granted in a separate illegal arms case linked to the pistol allegedly used in the shooting. The suspect spent nine days in physical custody and one day on judicial remand at Adiala jail before the court ruling.

Legal representatives for the defense and the Rawalpindi High Court Bar Association submitted the bail applications alongside the family's statements. The public prosecutor did not oppose the release, noting that legal heirs forgiving the accused in relation to diyat warrants granting bail. Investigators previously reported that polygraph examinations showed no signs of deception from Tahir, and forensic analysis confirmed a single shot was fired from the weapon.

The murder case was originally registered on November 8 at the Saddar Barooni police station following a complaint filed by the victim's brother. Senior Civil Journal Muhammad Nasrullah Wattoo instructed local police to submit the official challan by December 1. The family's statements are expected to be formally recorded again following the challan submission as legal proceedings continue.

stories.title: راولپنڈی ٹیسٹ: تیسرے روز کے اختتام پر سری لنکا کو پاکستان پر 82 رنز کی برتری حاصل
stories.summary:
راولپنڈی میں کھیلے جا رہے دوسرے کرکٹ ٹیسٹ کے تیسرے روز کا کھیل ختم ہونے پر سری لنکن ٹیم نے پاکستان کے خلاف 82 رنز کی سبقت حاصل کر لی ہے تاہم اس کی اننگز میں صرف ایک وکٹ باقی ہے۔ دن کے اختتام پر سری لنکا نے اپنی دوسری اننگز میں 9 وکٹوں کے نقصان پر 309 رنز بنا لیے تھے، اور کریز پر نصف سنچری بنانے والے ملن رتنائیکے اور اسیتھا فرنینڈو موجود ہیں۔

پاکستان کی جانب سے دوسری اننگز میں بولنگ کرتے ہوئے عامر جمال نے تین کھلاڑیوں کو آؤٹ کیا جو سب سے کامیاب بولر رہے۔ اس کے علاوہ محمد عباس اور رضا اللہ نے دو دو جبکہ سلمان علی آغا اور ثاقب خان نے ایک ایک وکٹ حاصل کی۔ پاکستانی ٹیم کو اس اننگز میں ثاقب خان کی خدمات مکمل طور پر حاصل نہ رہ سکیں کیونکہ وہ زخمی ہو کر اپنے دوسرے ہی اوور میں میدان سے باہر چلے گئے تھے۔

تیسرے دن سری لنکن بلے بازوں نے ذمہ دارانہ کھیل کا مظاہرہ کیا۔ ملن رتنائیکے کے علاوہ کپتان کشال مینڈس اور سونل دنوشا نے بھی نصف سنچریاں اسکور کیں، جن کی بہترین شراکت داری کی بدولت مہمان ٹیم پاکستان پر برتری حاصل کرنے میں کامیاب ہوئی۔ اس سے قبل پہلی اننگز میں سری لنکن ٹیم صرف 98 رنز پر ڈھیر ہو گئی تھی جس کے جواب میں پاکستان نے پہلی اننگز میں 325 رنز بنا کر 227 رنز کی بڑی برتری حاصل کی تھی۔

پہلی اننگز میں پاکستان کے فاسٹ بولرز نے شاندار کارکردگی دکھائی تھی جس میں محمد عباس، رضا اللہ اور عامر جمال نے تین تین جبکہ ثاقب خان نے ایک وکٹ حاصل کی تھی۔ دونوں ٹیموں کے درمیان پہلا ٹیسٹ میچ بے نتیجہ رہا تھا لہذا راولپنڈی کا یہ دوسرا ٹیسٹ میچ فیصلہ کن مرحلے میں داخل ہو چکا ہے اور جو بھی ٹیم یہ میچ جیتے گی، وہ سیریز اپنے نام کرنے میں کامیاب ہو جائے گی۔

stories.title: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif Credits Economic Progress to Civil-Military Partnership
stories.summary:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif stated that Pakistan's economic achievements stem from a collaborative partnership between the political leadership and the military hierarchy. Addressing an event organized by the American Business Council of Pakistan, he remarked that such teamwork had no precedent in the nation's history and contended that earlier cooperation of this nature could have transformed the country long ago.

Declining personal credit, the premier praised his administration and Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir alongside his team. He recalled that Pakistan faced a severe threat of economic default in 2023, but highlighted that the country currently maintains macroeconomic stability despite global pressures, including the Gulf crisis and challenges related to energy imports.

Prime Minister Sharif noted that over 90 percent of energy requirements are imported, yet the government avoided panic at fuel stations and introduced relief measures like the Prime Minister’s Fuel Relief Scheme for vulnerable segments. Furthermore, he mentioned that the administration provided Rs400 billion in tax breaks during the previous budget to stimulate exporters, manufacturers, and the salaried class despite being under an International Monetary Fund program.

Addressing regional and business matters, the prime minister stated that Pakistan is actively working with international partners to restore peace in the Middle East. He also reaffirmed the government's commitment to eliminating investment bottlenecks, improving transparency, and developing the nation's vast mineral deposits.

stories.title: راولپنڈی عدالت نے شوہر کو ضمانت پر رہا کر دیا
stories.summary:
پاکستان کے شہر راولپنڈی کی ایک مقامی عدالت نے اینکر پرسن ربیعہ احسن کے قتل کے مقدمے میں گرفتار ان کے شوہر کی ضمانت بعد از گرفتاری منظور کر لی ہے۔ ایڈیشنل ڈسٹرکٹ اینڈ سیشن جج خرم سلیم نے دو لاکھ روپے کے مچلکے کے عوض یہ حکم جاری کیا۔ سماعت کے دوران مقتولہ کے بھائی، والدہ اور بہن نے عدالت میں بیان حلفی جمع کروائے، جن میں مؤقف اختیار کیا گیا کہ واقعہ ایک حادثہ تھا اور انھیں ملزم کی رہائی پر کوئی اعتراض نہیں ہے۔

آٹھ نومبر کو گلشن آباد میں واقع رہائش گاہ سے اکیس سالہ ربیعہ احسن کی لاش برآمد ہوئی تھی، جن کے جسم پر گردن کے نیچے گولی لگنے کا نشان تھا۔ پولیس نے مقتولہ کے بھائی خرم احمد کی مدعیت میں تھانہ صدر بیرونی میں دفعہ 302 کے تحت مقدمہ درج کیا تھا اور موقع سے ایک بغیر لائسنس کا تیس بور پستول بھی برآمد کیا گیا تھا۔

ابتدائی تفتیش اور خرم احمد کے بیان کے مطابق، گھر کے اندر الماری سے کپڑے نکالتے وقت پستول اچانک چل گیا جس سے ربیعہ احسن موقع پر ہی جاں بحق ہو گئیں۔ پولیس اور فیملی کے مطابق اس واقعے سے قبل میاں بیوی کے درمیان کسی قسم کے گھریلو تنازع یا ناچاقی کی کوئی علامت موجود نہیں تھی۔

پولیس نے ابتدائی طور پر ملزم کا جسمانی اور جوڈیشل ریمانڈ حاصل کیا تھا اور تفتیش کے دوران ملزم کو پولی گرافک ٹیسٹ کے لیے لاہور بھی لے جایا گیا تھا۔ مقتولہ کے ورثا کے جانب سے بیان حلفی جمع کرائے جانے اور واقعے کو حادثہ قرار دینے کے بعد عدالت نے ضابطے کی کارروائی مکمل کرتے ہوئے ملزم کی ضمانت منظور کر لی ہے۔

stories.title: Pakistan Extends Airspace Ban on Indian Aircraft Until Late December
stories.summary:
Pakistan has extended its ongoing airspace restrictions for Indian aircraft through December 24. A Notice to Airmen issued by the Pakistan Airports Authority confirmed that the prohibition will remain in effect until 4:59 am on that date.

The restriction applies to all aircraft registered in India, as well as those owned, operated, or leased by Indian airlines. Additionally, the ban covers all Indian military flights across Pakistani airspace, continuing measures initially implemented following the 2025 Pahalgam attack in Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu and Kashmir.

The prolonged airspace closure has generated significant financial impacts for the aviation sector. Indian airlines have incurred millions of dollars in extra expenses by being forced to utilize alternative flight routes, which increase both travel time and fuel consumption for journeys connecting India with destinations in Europe, the Middle East, and Central Asia.

stories.title: Malaysian Palm Oil Futures Fall Over One Percent on Weak Dalian Prices
stories.summary:
Malaysian palm oil futures declined by more than one percent on Thursday, marking a third consecutive session of losses. The benchmark contract for February delivery on the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives Exchange decreased by 54 ringgit, translating to a 1.23% drop, to close at 4,332 ringgit, or $1,053.25, per metric ton.

The downturn was driven by heavy selling pressure aligned with declining prices in Dalian palm olein and soyoil. A broader bearish sentiment affected the entire edible oil complex during the trading day. Anilkumar Bagani, head of research at Sunvin Group, noted that the selloff in Dalian palm olein was exacerbated by historically high palm oil inventories in China. Furthermore, a narrowing discount against gasoil has negatively impacted the demand for palm oil in biofuel manufacturing.

In related markets, Dalian’s most-active soyoil contract dropped 1.43% and its palm oil contract fell 3.01%. Conversely, Chicago Board of Trade soyoil prices increased by 0.62%. Palm oil typically tracks competing edible oil prices as it vies for market share globally.

Crude oil prices experienced a slight increase following earlier losses, supported by supply concerns in the Middle East stemming from shipping attacks in the Strait of Hormuz, which balanced expectations of a market surplus. Higher crude oil futures improve the appeal of palm oil as a biodiesel feedstock. Meanwhile, the ringgit rose 0.05% against the US dollar, making the commodity slightly more expensive for international buyers holding foreign currencies.

stories.title: Prime Minister Shehbaz Credits Military-Political Partnership for Economic Stability
stories.summary:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif stated on Thursday that Pakistan's recent economic achievements are the result of an unprecedented and productive partnership between the nation's political and military leadership. He emphasized that teamwork has been essential for achieving national stability.

Speaking at an event hosted by the American Business Council of Pakistan in Islamabad, the prime minister outlined several key economic indicators. He noted that Pakistan has maintained stability despite the global shocks caused by the Gulf crisis, which heavily impacted powerful economies worldwide.

Sharif pointed out that Pakistan imports over 90% of its energy needs, including oil, gas, liquefied natural gas, and petrol. Despite this high vulnerability in energy requirements, he emphasized that the country has avoided public unrest at petrol pumps while successfully implementing subsidy programs to protect vulnerable populations.

Addressing the business community directly, the prime minister reiterated that these accomplishments would have been impossible without collective efforts and teamwork. He stated that the level of cooperation currently seen between the military and political hierarchy is entirely unique in the history of Pakistan.

stories.title: MQM-P Chief Urges Judicial Action Over Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari's Bloodshed Remark
stories.summary:
Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P) chief Dr Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui called on the courts on Thursday to take notice of recent remarks made by PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari. The controversy arose after Bilawal warned during a speech that dividing Sindh would cause blood to flow through its streets.

During a press conference in Karachi, Siddiqui criticized the PPP chairman's remarks, arguing that political parties should respond with arguments rather than threats. He described the current political landscape as a feudalistic democracy where leaders emerge from dynastic backgrounds rather than grassroots political work. Siddiqui questioned why Bilawal's predicted bloodshed would be concentrated in urban areas like Karachi, Hyderabad, Mirpurkhas, and Nawabshah if MQM-P's demand for new administrative provinces applied nationwide.

Siddiqui also alleged that the PPP's resistance to new provinces stems from the fact that Karachi generates 97 percent of Sindh's provincial budget. He criticized the governance and development record in Sindh, claiming that development functions merely as a byproduct of corruption. Additionally, he noted that the PPP holds governance roles in multiple regions including Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Gilgit-Baltistan, and Balochistan.

Concluding his address, Siddiqui stated that MQM-P respects Bilawal's mandate and has chosen not to engage in physical conflict, opting instead for constitutional and legal battles. He reiterated his appeal to both the federal government and the judiciary to take notice of Bilawal's statements and insisted that threats have no place in their political discourse.

stories.title: Pakistan Extends Airspace Ban on Indian Aircraft Until December 23
stories.summary:
Pakistan has prolonged its airspace ban on Indian-registered aircraft, as well as planes owned, operated, or leased by Indian carriers and military flights, until December 23. A Notice to Airmen issued by the Pakistan Airports Authority confirmed that the restriction will remain active until 23:59 on that date across both the Karachi and Lahore flight information regions.

The airspace restrictions were originally implemented in late April 2025 following a surge in bilateral tensions triggered by a deadly attack in Pahalgam, located in India-occupied Kashmir. New Delhi attributed the attack to Islamabad without providing evidence, a claim strongly denied by Pakistan, which offered a neutral investigation. Relations deteriorated further in May during an intense aerial engagement.

The ongoing closures have forced Indian airlines to divert to longer and more expensive flight paths. Air India, which operates a major international network, previously reported significant financial and operational impacts, noting substantial increases in fuel costs and journey times on long-haul routes alongside a multimillion-dollar hit to its annual profit before tax.

stories.title: Pakistan High Commission in London Restores Consular Services After Outage
stories.summary:
The Pakistan High Commission in London has officially announced the complete restoration of NADRA, passport, and visa services following technical difficulties caused by an international internet disruption. Officials confirmed that all affected consular operations are now functioning normally according to their regular schedules.

The disruption had temporarily impacted specific consular functions at the diplomatic mission. With the technical problems resolved, all facilities have been successfully reactivated to serve the public once again.

The High Commission further stated that all previously scheduled appointments remain valid and will not be canceled or altered because of the recent outage. Applicants who already secured appointments are strongly advised to visit the mission on their designated dates and times.

This restoration of services aims to assist Pakistani nationals residing across the United Kingdom who depend on timely identity documentation, passport renewals, and visa assistance. The mission has urged all individuals to adhere strictly to their existing appointment schedules as normal operations resume.

stories.title: Sindh Advisor Urges Agencies to Finish Drought Survey in Tharparkar
stories.summary:
Provincial Advisor Gianchand Essarani presided over a meeting in Karachi focusing on the drought conditions in the Tharparkar region. During the session, he called upon United Nations agencies to expedite and complete a comprehensive survey of the drought-stricken areas within the district.

Essarani emphasized the necessity of effective relief measures tailored to the actual needs of the affected population. He highlighted the importance of strong coordination among government departments, district administrations, and humanitarian organizations. Furthermore, he asked the International Organization for Migration to review water supply project efforts in Tharparkar and Umarkot, and urged the World Food Programme to examine school feeding initiatives for children.

The region has been officially declared drought-hit after agricultural crops suffered widespread destruction, leading to critical water and fodder shortages that impact both farming and livestock. Government sources indicate that roughly 85 to 90 percent of crops across all seven talukas in Tharparkar have been completely destroyed or rendered unproductive.

Providing drinking water, food, and other basic necessities remains the government's foremost priority for the area. A recently initiated survey is set to comprehensively review critical issues including food availability, clean water access, education, maternal and child health, and livestock welfare.

stories.title: Protests and Arson Shake Bangladesh Ahead of Hasina's Return
stories.summary:
Supporters of ousted former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina staged demonstrations across Bangladesh, resulting in widespread violence and an arson attack on the ancestral home of former interim leader Muhammad Yunus in Chittagong. The blaze caused no casualties, but authorities blamed the incident on members of Hasina's banned Awami League party. The unrest comes ahead of Hasina's planned return from exile in India next December, despite her facing a death sentence.

Security forces have responded firmly to the escalating turmoil. Border Guard Bangladesh deployed hundreds of paramilitary troops across seven districts, including Hasina's hometown of Gopalganj, where multiple arson incidents have occurred. Protesters recently set fire to a local police station and a lawmaker's home, while clashes resulted in the deaths of two ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party activists. Police report that 107 arrests have been made since Wednesday, and former education minister Nurul Islam Nahid has also been detained in connection with past protests.

The political crisis stems from the 2024 student-led uprising that forced Hasina from power, after which a court sentenced the 79-year-old former leader to death in absentia for crimes against humanity. Hasina has nonetheless vowed to return, stating she is fully aware of the risks. Meanwhile, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has urged national unity among democratic forces to counter ongoing efforts to destabilize the country of 170 million people.

stories.title: Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari Advocates Political Inclusion for Imran Khan
stories.summary:
Pakistan Peoples Party chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari has publicly described Imran Khan as a political prisoner and urged an end to political victimisation. Speaking at a press conference in Karachi, Bilawal argued that excluding a major political party from the democratic process prevents the country from functioning properly and called for a political reset involving the government, opposition, and judiciary.

Although the PPP is a coalition partner with the PML-N-led federal federal government, Bilawal has increasingly distanced himself from certain government policies. His recent criticisms of proposed judicial reforms, constitutional amendments, and the handling of opposition grievances have sparked friction with federal leaders. Defense Minister Khawaja Asif publicly responded by questioning the PPP's positioning while it remains part of the governing coalition.

Despite his defense of political rights and parliamentary inclusion for the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf, analysts note that Bilawal's stance does not constitute a formal political alliance. Bilawal has previously criticized PTI's confrontational tactics and urged them to engage constructively within Parliament. By championing dialogue and political reconciliation, the PPP appears to be carving out independent political space and appealing to voters weary of ongoing instability.

stories.title: Saudi Foreign Minister and Makkah Defence Alliance Chief Discuss Defence Ties
stories.summary:
Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan met with Nauman Mahmood, the Secretary-General of the Makkah Defence Alliance, in Riyadh to review institutional development and strengthen defence coordination among member states. The discussions focused on advancing coordination mechanisms within the General Secretariat to reinforce their joint defence framework.

The high-level talks occurred shortly after Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan noted that Türkiye would welcome new members to the alliance once its institutional structure is established, provided they respect international law and seek regional peace. The Makkah Defence Alliance itself originated from an agreement signed in Makkah on August 7 by Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, designed to boost deterrence and collective defence by treating an attack on one member as an attack on all three.

Following an emergency meeting in Riyadh on October 5, the founding nations decided to immediately enact their collective defence commitments and appointed Mahmood as the organization's inaugural secretary-general for a three-year term. Earlier this month, the Turkish parliament officially approved legislation allowing the formal ratification of the pact.

This diplomatic engagement underscores the continued operational rollout of the trilateral alliance as member nations build up their institutional framework and cooperation mechanisms. Enhancing joint military readiness and collective security remains a central priority for the participating leadership as the regional pact solidifies its foundation.

stories.title: Pakistani Security Forces Eliminate 22 Terrorists in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
stories.summary:
Security forces in Pakistan neutralized 22 India-backed terrorists during a series of operations across the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, according to the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR). The military's media wing stated that the engagements took place between November 16 and 17, 2026. Troops carried out an intelligence-based operation in the South Waziristan district, engaging a militant location that resulted in an intense exchange of fire and the killing of fifteen individuals linked to the Indian-sponsored Fitna al-Khawarij group. 

Additional encounters unfolded in the Bannu and Tank districts. In Bannu, security forces targeted militant hideouts and successfully eliminated six terrorists, while another insurgent was killed during a separate clash in Tank. Authorities also recovered various weapons and ammunition from the dead combatants, who had been actively involved in numerous violent incidents within the region. Following these engagements, sanitation operations were initiated to sweep the area for any remaining threats.

The military emphasized its dedication to pursuing a relentless counterterrorism campaign designed to completely root out foreign-sponsored and supported terrorism from the nation. Pakistan has experienced a notable escalation in militant violence since the Afghan Taliban assumed power in 2021, with Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan emerging as the primary centers of conflict.

Data from a report by the Centre for Research and Security Studies (CRSS) covering the second quarter of 2026 highlights the severity of the security situation in these two provinces. Together, KP and Balochistan accounted for approximately 96% of all violence-related fatalities nationwide during that period. Specifically, KP recorded more than 61% of the total deaths, amounting to 475 fatalities, alongside 151 violent incidents, which constituted 57% of the total recorded across the country.

stories.title: International Court of Justice Rules Myanmar Committed State-Sponsored Rohingya Genocide
stories.summary:
The International Court of Justice (ICJ) in The Hague delivered a landmark ruling on Thursday, finding Myanmar responsible for state-sponsored genocide against its Muslim Rohingya minority population during 2017 military operations in Rakhine State. Decided by a 9-6 majority, the historic verdict marks the first time the UN's top court has held a sovereign state accountable for genocide, following a case initiated by Gambia under the 1948 Genocide Convention.

Judges concluded that the military operations featured extreme scale and methods that exceeded necessity, revealing a clear intent to destroy a substantial portion of the Rohingya population amid mass killings, sexual violence, and the displacement of over 700,000 individuals to Bangladesh. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres strongly welcomed the binding, final, and unappealable judgment, praising it as vital recognition for victims and a crucial step toward ending impunity and fostering durable peace in Myanmar.

UN human rights chief Volker Turk also applauded the decision, urging Myanmar to immediately implement the court-mandated remedies and calling on international actors to halt military equipment and jet fuel transfers. Turk further cautioned against premature repatriation, emphasizing that displaced Rohingya must only return when safe and sustainable conditions are established, while urging countries to reevaluate ties with Myanmar's authorities.

Global and local reactions swiftly followed the verdict, with Myanmar's shadow National Unity Government acknowledging the court's authority and human rights commitments. Activists and survivors, including Rohingya delegate Yasmin Ullah, hailed the ruling as a long-awaited acknowledgment by the world's highest court, validating the immense suffering endured by the community during the military crackdowns.

stories.title: Election Commission of Pakistan Establishes University Consortium for Electoral Research
stories.summary: The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) has formed a partnership with 19 universities nationwide to foster democratic awareness and electoral research. According to ECP member Nisar Ahmed Durrani, memorandums of understanding have already been finalized with 13 of these institutions for a duration of three years. This initiative aims to boost youth engagement in the electoral system while allowing the commission to utilize academic research capabilities to tackle various election-related challenges. As part of these agreements, participating universities will introduce a student ambassadorship program alongside internship opportunities directly at the ECP. In a separate development, the Pakistan High Commission in London announced that consular services, including passports, visas, and NADRA operations, have fully resumed following technical issues triggered by an international internet outage.

stories.title: South Africa Defeats Bangladesh by Nine Wickets in First Test at Wanderers
stories.summary: South Africa secured a convincing nine-wicket victory over Bangladesh on Thursday in the first Test match at the Wanderers in Johannesburg. The win advances South Africa in the two-match series and strengthens their position for a spot in the upcoming World Test Championship final in London next year. Bangladesh, having won the toss and batted first to score 400 runs, were bowled out for 168 in their second innings, leaving South Africa a target of just 12 runs. Off-spinner Simon Harmer claimed six wickets for 51 runs, while Kagiso Rabada contributed three wickets for 48 runs. Despite losing opener Marques Ackerman on the very first ball, South Africa quickly chased down the target before lunch. Bangladesh's Litton Das top-scored in the second innings with 39 runs and previously broke the record for most dismissals by a wicketkeeper in a Test innings with eight. South African captain Temba Bavuma noted that his team's ability to bounce back is both a strength and a weakness, and he may miss the upcoming second Test in Centurion due to a calf injury. With this result, South Africa has claimed 16 victories from their last 18 Tests and moved to the top of the World Test Championship standings.

stories.title: Indian Rupee Reaches Seven-Month High Driven by Local Stock Market Rally
stories.summary: The Indian rupee appreciated by 0.16% on Thursday to conclude trading at 93.29 per dollar, marking its strongest performance in seven months. This currency movement was propelled by a one percent increase in India's benchmark Nifty 50 stock index. Throughout November, the Nifty 50 has climbed more than ten percent, driven by an influx of foreign equity investments into domestic markets, which has in turn lifted the rupee by roughly 1.8 percent for the month. The surge in foreign capital has alleviated pressure on the central bank, enabling a significant reduction in its dollar sales after months of heavy market intervention. Financial analysts and traders are now closely monitoring whether export-related dollar conversions will increase to sustain the rupee's upward momentum. Deutsche Bank analysts noted that a drop below the 93 threshold could trigger substantial exporter conversions of US dollar holdings. Meanwhile, corporate participation remains mixed, with some financial lenders reporting higher exporter activity while others observe continuous importer hedging. Globally, the dollar index declined by 0.1 percent to 103.7, and market attention later shifted to the market debut of Anthropic, the maker of the Claude chatbot.

stories.title: Pakistani Rupee Edges Up Against US Dollar Amid Global Rate Hike Signals
stories.summary: The Pakistani rupee experienced a marginal appreciation of 0.01% in the inter-bank market on Thursday, closing at 276.52 against the US dollar compared to 276.55 on the previous day. Globally, the greenback remained near a 19-month high following the release of Federal Reserve meeting minutes and hawkish commentary from officials suggesting the possibility of further interest rate increases. Minutes from the October 27-28 meeting revealed growing concern among officials regarding inflation control, while Fed Governor Christopher Waller proposed either a 50-basis-point rate hike in December or accelerated tightening in 2027. This strong US currency placed pressure on other global currencies, pushing the Australian dollar to a ten-month low following weak employment figures and driving the euro and sterling lower. In commodity markets, oil prices stabilized after earlier losses, with Brent crude rising slightly to $92 a barrel and West Texas Intermediate futures declining to $83, as market participants weighed market surplus expectations against Middle East supply concerns.

stories.title: Indian Equities Rise on Auto and Financial Strength Amid Wider Asian Slump
stories.summary:
Indian financial markets defied a broader regional downturn on Thursday, driven by robust gains in the automotive and financial sectors. The Nifty 50 advanced 1.14% to 25,514.30, while the Sensex climbed 1.21% to 83,021.75. This performance contrasted with MSCI’s broadest Asia-Pacific index outside Japan, which fell 1.7% amid cautious sentiment over artificial intelligence trades and hawkish messages from the US Federal Reserve.

The ongoing rally is largely fueled by a reversal of foreign capital flows back to India, supported by record monthly foreign inflows totaling $11.28 billion in November. Analysts note that solid corporate earnings and a 21.6% drop in crude oil prices are underpinning positive market perspectives despite narrowing valuation cushions. Small-cap and mid-cap indexes also recorded increases of approximately 0.7% and 1.1%, respectively.

Among major sectors, the auto index jumped 4.4% due to easing commodity expenses and strong festival demand, with Maruti Suzuki India leading Nifty gainers with a 7.6% surge. Banking and financial counters advanced between 1.1% and 2.3%. Conversely, information technology companies formed the sole declining sector, dropping 1.1% following US Federal Reserve meeting minutes indicating a stronger focus on curbing inflation, which raised concerns over US client technology spending.

Online-payment providers such as Paytm, One Mobikwik, and Pine Labs also registered losses between 4.8% and 8.7%. The gains in broader sectors highlight resilient domestic economic drivers that helped local indices outperform regional trends.

stories.title: Pakistan Electoral Reforms Panel Formation Stalls Over Missing Opposition Nominees
stories.summary:
The establishment of the Parliamentary Committee on Electoral Reforms in Pakistan has hit delays as the opposition has yet to provide its designated representatives. Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry announced the setback on Thursday following discussions with opposition chief whip Malik Amir Dogar. Chaudhry stated that government allied parties have already submitted their choices, and the National Assembly Speaker will issue the official notification as soon as the remaining names are furnished.

The minister urged the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf party to join the panel and voice its positions officially rather than airing grievances in media appearances or assembly floor speeches. He noted that constructive proposals from the party would be integrated into the electoral framework draft, offering a platform to discuss upcoming general elections and the broader political climate. Meanwhile, PTI leaders explained that decisions regarding participation require a formal parliamentary party meeting, which has faced scheduling delays.

PTI representatives emphasized that they aim to maintain equal representation within the committee, echoing the structure of the 2017 reform process to prevent unilateral decision-making. Party officials noted that while founding chairman Imran Khan previously instructed members to avoid standard parliamentary committees, he has not issued specific directives concerning this particular electoral reform body. Consultations with party leadership and coalition partners, including Mahmood Khan Achakzai and Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, are scheduled to take place shortly.

Earlier in the month, the government initiated steps to bring all political factions to the negotiating table by reaching out to allies like the PPP and the MQM-P for nominations. While the administration seeks inclusive dialogue on election procedures, opposition figures had initially labeled the initiative a futile endeavor unless their core demands are addressed.

stories.title: South Africa Defeats Bangladesh by Nine Wickets in Opening Test Match
stories.summary:
South Africa secured a commanding nine-wicket victory over Bangladesh on Thursday to claim the first Test of the series at the Wanderers Stadium. Off-spinner Simon Harmer delivered a stellar bowling performance, taking six wickets for 51 runs to dismantle the opposition batting lineup as Bangladesh was dismissed for 168 in their second innings.

Resuming the final day at 100 for five, Bangladesh initially showed resilience through a 34-run partnership between Litton Das and Mushfiqur Rahim across seven overs. The resistance ended when Kagiso Rabada bowled Das for 39 runs. Harmer then claimed the remaining four wickets, utilizing sharp turn from a wearing pitch to quickly wrap up the innings.

Chasing a target of just 12 runs for victory, the defending champions needed only 1.3 overs to secure the win. The triumph propelled South Africa to the summit of the current World Test Championship standings. During the brief chase, Aiden Markram hit a six off Ebadot Hossain and was bowled on the next delivery, but survived due to a no-call before hitting the winning run.

Bangladesh had previously scored 400 runs in their first innings, while South Africa's earlier efforts featured first-innings top-scorer Marques Ackerman. With this outcome, South Africa establishes a 1-0 lead in the two-match series.

stories.title: HRCP Condemns Punjab Dramatic Performances Bill Over Free Speech Threats
stories.summary:
The Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP) has strongly criticized the newly passed Punjab Dramatic and Theatrical Performances Bill 2026, warning that the legislation severely undermines artistic freedom and shields the government from public criticism. The controversial bill was passed by the Punjab Assembly following intense confrontations between treasury and opposition benches concerning theatre regulations and performance oversight.

According to the HRCP, the law effectively places the administration beyond satire and public critique by prohibiting performances deemed likely to generate disaffection toward the government. The organization labeled these provisions a gross violation of fundamental rights to free expression and artistic liberty. Furthermore, the commission raised serious objections to mandatory licensing requirements, government-controlled script reviews, and institutionalized censorship backed by potential fines and imprisonment.

Specific language within Article 3 of the legislation bans dramatic or theatrical performances that are scandalous, defamatory, obscene, vulgar, likely to incite religious hatred, or prone to inciting feelings of disaffection against the government. These broad prohibitions have sparked widespread concern regarding cultural suppression and state overreach into creative expression.

In response to the legislative development, the HRCP announced plans to host consultations with artists and key stakeholders. The upcoming meetings will evaluate the broader implications of the statute and determine appropriate measures to protect cultural freedoms across the region.

stories.title: ایس ای سی پی نے موبائل ایپس کے ڈیجیٹل قرضوں پر شرح منافع کم کر دی
stories.summary:
سکیورٹیز اینڈ ایکسچینج کمیشن آف پاکستان (ایس ای سی پی) نے موبائل ایپلی کیشنز کے ذریعے دیے جانے والے مختصر مدت اور کم مالیت کے ڈیجیٹل نینو قرضوں پر سالانہ شرحِ منافع میں نمایاں کمی کا اعلان کیا ہے۔ اس اقدام کا مقصد کم آمدنی والے صارفین کو مالی بوجھ سے بچانا اور ڈیجیٹل قرضوں کے شعبے کو زیادہ شفاف بنانا ہے۔

نئے سرکلر کے تحت نینو قرضوں کی سالانہ لاگت کی زیادہ سے زیادہ حد 274 فیصد سے گھٹا کر نئے صارفین کے لیے 90 فیصد اور بروقت پرانے قرض چکانے والوں کے لیے 70 فیصد مقرر کر دی گئی ہے۔ ایک صارف زیادہ سے زیادہ پچاس ہزار روپے تک کا قرض نوے دن تک کی مدت کے لیے حاصل کر سکے گا، جبکہ قبل از وقت ادائیگی کی صورت میں صرف استعمال شدہ دنوں کے چارجز وصول کیے جائیں گے۔

ایس ای سی پی کے نئے ضوابط میں یہ بھی واضح کیا گیا ہے کہ قرض کی مدت خودکار طور پر نہیں بڑھائی جائے گی اور مقررہ تاریخ کے بعد ابتدائی تین روز تک کوئی تاخیرانہ جرمانہ وصول نہیں ہوگا۔ اس کے علاوہ کمیشن ایک مرکزی ڈیجیٹل ریکارڈ قائم کرنے پر بھی کام کر رہا ہے تاکہ صارفین کی مالی استطاعت کا بہتر اندازہ لگایا جا سکے۔

مالیاتی ماہرین کے مطابق ڈیجیٹل نینو قرضوں پر شرح منافع زیادہ ہونے کی بنیادی وجہ بغیر ضمانت کے قرض فراہم کرنے کا 'ڈیفالٹ رسک' ہے۔ تاہم ریگولیٹر نے تمام لائسنس یافتہ اداروں کو پندرہ دن کے اندر اپنی ایپس اور شرائط نئے قواعد کے مطابق اپ ڈیٹ کرنے کی سخت ہدایت جاری کی ہے۔

stories.title: Oil Prices Inch Up Amid Middle East Shipping Attacks and Market Surpluses
stories.summary:
Oil prices experienced a slight increase on Thursday, recovering somewhat from losses during the previous session. Brent crude futures rose by 24 cents, reaching $92.19 a barrel by 0953 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate futures for December climbed 5 cents to $83.31. The price movements were driven by opposing market forces, as ongoing security concerns in the Middle East countered expectations of a supply surplus.

Geopolitical tensions continued to influence the energy sector. According to Iranian media reports on Wednesday, three oil tankers sailing east of the Strait of Hormuz were disabled by mines. Meanwhile, the Houthi movement fired missiles at the Saudi Arabian capital of Riyadh on Thursday, though the Saudi Civil Defense agency confirmed the danger had passed. US President Donald Trump, along with his Chinese and Russian counterparts Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, held a trilateral meeting where Trump emphasized the critical need to keep oil flowing through the Strait of Hormuz. Additionally, Ukrainian drone attacks have slashed Russian oil refineries' combined crude processing volumes by 45% since late October.

Despite these supply risks, several factors weighed on the market outlook. The US Energy Information Administration reported that domestic crude inventories rose by 3.4 million barrels to 417.8 million barrels for the week ending November 13, well above analysts' expectations of a 58,000-barrel increase. Furthermore, expectations of higher US interest rates have put downward pressure on prices by threatening to slow economic growth, dampen oil demand, and strengthen the dollar, which increases costs for non-US buyers.

These market dynamics come as Brent and WTI previously suffered declines, with WTI hitting its lowest point since August 26. Analysts note that while persistent disruptions in regions like Ukraine and the Middle East maintain elevated risks for energy infrastructure and exports, growing US stockpiles and macroeconomic pressures continue to introduce uncertainty regarding future price trajectories.

stories.title: Pakistan and Asean Explore Expanded Trade and Investment Opportunities
stories.summary:
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar held delegation-level talks with the Secretary General of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean), Dr. Kao Kim Hourn, at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on November 19. Dr. Hourn is visiting Pakistan on a working trip from November 18 to 20, marking the first high-level visit to the country from the Asean Secretariat.

During the discussions, both officials reviewed ongoing progress under the Pakistan-Asean Sectoral Dialogue Partnership. The talks centered on expanding bilateral trade and investment, strengthening regional connectivity, and enhancing cooperation in agriculture, food security, climate resilience, disaster preparedness, and digital innovation. DPM Dar highlighted the potential for closer connections between business communities in Pakistan and Asean member states, while also stressing the importance of scholarships, student exchanges, and joint research to build stronger people-to-people ties.

The meeting also provided an opportunity for both sides to exchange perspectives on regional developments. Dr. Hourn acknowledged Pakistan's constructive role in promoting regional peace and stability, and DPM Dar reaffirmed the country's dedication to collaborating closely with the Asean Secretariat and its member nations to advance their shared partnership.

Pakistan has maintained a formal relationship with the bloc as an Asean Sectoral Dialogue Partner since 1993 and has been a member of the Asean Regional Forum since 2004. Founded on August 8, 1967, via the Bangkok Declaration by Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, and Thailand, Asean currently comprises 11 member states. This high-level visit underscores a mutual commitment between Pakistan and Asean to deepen and diversify their cooperative ties across multiple sectors.

stories.title: Gold Prices in Pakistan Decrease Following International Market Drop
stories.summary:
Gold prices in Pakistan experienced a downward adjustment on Thursday, moving in tandem with a decline observed in the international market. According to rates provided by the All-Pakistan Gems and Jewellers Sarafa Association, the price of gold per tola decreased by Rs3,700, settling at Rs395,236.

In addition to the per tola drop, the price for 10 grams of gold fell by Rs3,172, bringing it to a value of Rs338,851. This downward trend followed a previous session on Wednesday when the per tola price had already dropped by Rs10,000 to reach Rs398,936. The local market shifts directly reflected global trends, where the international rate of gold declined by $37, reaching $3,727 per ounce.

Alongside the precious yellow metal, the local market also saw a decrease in silver prices. Silver dropped by Rs43 during the session, bringing its new rate to Rs5,005 per tola.

These fluctuations demonstrate how closely the domestic bullion market in Pakistan tracks international pricing movements. Jewellers and investors continue to monitor global commodity shifts as local rates fluctuate in response to international economic indicators and foreign market demand.

stories.title: Millions of inDrive Users in Pakistan Utilize Ride-Sharing Safety Feature
stories.summary:
As digital mobility expands across Pakistan, safety remains a primary concern for commuters relying on ride-hailing applications. inDrive, operating on a peer-to-peer model that allows passengers and drivers to negotiate fair fares directly without penalties, has integrated digital safety tools to address commuter security. Internal analytics reveal that over 8.8 million inDrive users in Pakistan utilized the platform's "Share Your Ride" feature between April and September 2026.

The "Share Your Ride" feature allows passengers to instantly share active trip details with trusted friends or family members via messaging apps or social links. Once shared, contacts can monitor the journey in real time by tracking the vehicle's exact route, current status, and live location updates from pickup until the trip concludes. This tool provides reassurance for passengers, particularly during late-night travels or when navigating unfamiliar routes across busy urban areas.

This feature forms part of a broader technological shift toward proactive safety measures within the platform. inDrive incorporates an artificial intelligence framework that moves away from purely reactive safety responses. The system analyzes data signals across driver and vehicle verification, in-app communications, ride details, and post-trip feedback to identify anomalies and assess risks instantly. Human safety specialists also review critical flags to ensure reliable oversight alongside automated algorithms.

The widespread adoption of these digital tools highlights a cultural shift among urban commuters, who increasingly expect transparent and accessible safety features from ride-hailing services. By combining a transparent economic model with AI-driven preventive technologies and easy-to-use tracking tools, inDrive continues to shape urban mobility standards throughout Pakistan.

stories.title: Xi, Trump, and Putin Hold Historic Trilateral Summit in Shenzhen
stories.summary:
The leaders of China, the United States, and Russia convened for an unprecedented trilateral meeting on Thursday on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen. Chinese President Xi Jinping, US President Donald Trump, and Russian President Vladimir Putin gathered at Kylin Villa for talks that Beijing stated were intended to safeguard world peace, though the gathering drew international skepticism and concern.

The summit occurred against the backdrop of major global conflicts, including Russia's ongoing military campaign in Ukraine nearing its fifth year and a US-Iran war that has disrupted global oil supplies and driven up consumer prices. Critics warned that the high-level meeting might signal an effort by the three powers to divide the globe into distinct spheres of influence, potentially impacting European and Ukrainian interests without direct participation.

Prior to the three-way discussions, Trump and Putin held bilateral talks where Trump referred to Putin as a friend, marking their first meeting since August 2025. Trump also engaged in separate one-on-one discussions with Xi, highlighting a special relationship centered on trade and potential artificial intelligence frameworks. Additional agenda items for the leaders included nuclear disarmament discussions, following the expiration of a bilateral arms treaty in February, alongside the ongoing situation in Iran.

The diplomatic optics drew sharp criticism from domestic opponents in the United States, who argued the summit legitimizes Russian actions in Ukraine and disadvantages American diplomatic standing. Meanwhile, all participating leaders, including Putin, concluded the summit events by posing together for the traditional APEC family photograph in designated ceremonial scarves.

stories.title: Dakota and Elle Fanning Star as Sisters in Trailer for WWII Film 'The Nightingale'
stories.summary:
Sony Pictures has unveiled the official trailer for the upcoming Second World War drama "The Nightingale," which features real-life siblings Dakota and Elle Fanning sharing the screen as adult co-stars for the first time. Based on Kristin Hannah's bestselling novel, the cinematic adaptation is slated to hit movie theaters on March 19.

Set against the backdrop of Nazi-occupied France, the narrative follows two sisters as they undertake separate, perilous journeys to navigate the dangers of wartime occupation while fighting for their survival and freedom. Elle Fanning takes on the character Isabelle Rossignol, whereas Dakota Fanning portrays Vianne Mauriac, with both siblings becoming actively involved in the resistance movement against Nazi Germany.

The supporting cast features notable actors including Edmund Donovan, Shira Haas as Rachel de Champlain, Mark Rylance as Julien Rossignol, Albrecht Schuch, Douglas Hodge, Gwilym Lee, and Vinette Robinson. Michael Morris directed the film from a screenplay penned jointly by Dana Stevens and Ann Peacock.

Production of the project was managed by the Fanning sisters alongside Reese Witherspoon, Brittany Kahan Ward, Lauren Neustadter, and Elizabeth Cantillon, with author Kristin Hannah contributing as an executive producer. Although the sisters previously appeared together in the 2001 film "I Am Sam," this release marks their debut starring roles together as adults.

stories.title: Somalia Expels UAE Ambassador and Recalls Envoy Over Sovereignty Dispute
stories.summary:
Somalia has ordered the ambassador of the United Arab Emirates to leave the country within 72 hours while simultaneously withdrawing its own envoy from Abu Dhabi. Information Minister Abdifatah Kasim Mohamud announced the decision during a state-run broadcast, labeling the actions of the UAE as an open invasion and a violation of national sovereignty. The government warned that strict measures would be taken against anyone cooperating with the UAE in what it described as an assault on Somali security, land, and unity.

The diplomatic fallout follows recent tensions highlighted by President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, who accused the Emirates of providing economic and political support to regional Somali governments to challenge the federal authority. In January, Mogadishu announced the cancellation of all agreements with the UAE, including port deals and defense cooperation pacts, though three self-governing Somali regions rejected that move.

The UAE has a history of involvement in Somalia, having funded and trained hundreds of troops between 2014 and 2018. While the UAE has long denied interfering in internal affairs, it continues to cover salaries and provide logistical support for approximately 3,400 Somali military police and special forces in and around the capital. The UAE has also invested hundreds of millions of dollars into coastal ports and military infrastructure along vital global shipping routes in the Horn of Africa.

This diplomatic crisis matters because it deepens instability in a nation where the federal government has historically struggled to assert authority and defeat militants, despite years of international assistance and peacekeepers. The escalating rift between Mogadishu and Abu Dhabi threatens regional alliances and underscores broader geopolitical competition for influence along critical maritime trade corridors.

stories.title: Australian Test Captain Pat Cummins Faces Scrutiny Following New Ball-Tampering Claims
stories.summary:
Australia Test cricket captain Pat Cummins is facing intense scrutiny and calls for his leadership to be reviewed after Cameron Bancroft renewed allegations regarding the infamous 2018 ball-tampering scandal in South Africa. Bancroft released a detailed newspaper column asserting that the entire squad was aware of the illicit plot involving sandpaper during a Test match in Cape Town, directly challenging Cummins' recent denials. The 2018 incident previously resulted in disgrace, bans, and repatriation for Bancroft, alongside then-captain Steve Smith and vice-captain David Warner, following an official Cricket Australia investigation that pinned responsibility solely on those three individuals.

Bancroft stated that he felt angry and betrayed by Cummins' recent public rebuttals, which were prompted by similar claims made in an autobiography by Usman Khawaja. In his new account, Bancroft also implicated David Warner as the person who initially brought up using sandpaper during the second Test in Port Elizabeth, and claimed that coaches Darren Lehmann and David Saker were present during discussions about the plan. Lehmann has since denied any prior knowledge of the scheme, noting he needs time to process the fresh allegations. Meanwhile, Bancroft expressed a sense of emotional relief and freedom after coming forward with his story, though he declined to comment when asked whether Cummins should step down from his role.

In defense of the captain, Neil Maxwell, Cummins' manager, released a statement emphasizing that Cummins has remained consistent and adamant regarding his stance over the past eight years. Maxwell noted that Cummins, who was a 24-year-old player in Cape Town, has spent nearly a decade working to rebuild the national squad. Despite these assurances, major media outlets such as The Australian, the ABC, and the Sydney Morning Herald have published editorials arguing that Cummins' future as Test captain is now in jeopardy and should be evaluated immediately.

Amid the growing controversy, Cummins returned to training alongside teammate Josh Hazlewood ahead of an upcoming Sheffield Shield fixture, choosing to remain silent on the matter. The announcement of Australia's squad for the home Test series against New Zealand, scheduled for December and January, has been delayed from its anticipated release this week. Prior to Bancroft's latest statements, Cricket Australia chief executive Todd Greenberg stated that the organization would not reopen its 2018 inquiry, opting instead to establish a forum for players to discuss their past experiences, while maintaining that Cummins' account of events was not under scrutiny.

stories.title: Army Chief Munir Inspects Troops and Reviews Security in Turbat
stories.summary:
Field Marshal Asim Munir, serving as both Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces, travelled to Turbat to inspect troops and evaluate their operational readiness and professionalism under difficult conditions. The Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) reported that the military leader received a detailed briefing regarding the local security climate, preparedness measures, and ongoing missions targeting externally backed terrorism upon his arrival in the city.

Upon landing, the army chief was greeted by the Corps Commander Balochistan. He subsequently paid his respects by laying a floral wreath at the Shuhada Monument and offering fateha. During his discussions with military personnel, Field Marshal Munir praised their steadfast determination to protect the country and reiterated the Pakistan Army's ongoing support for the residents of Balochistan in their quest for regional peace, economic prosperity, and sustainable development. Additionally, he was updated on the status of various socio-economic development programs aimed at benefiting the local population.

This visit follows a recent violent incident in Balochistan's Kolpur area on November 14, where India-backed terrorists utilized armed quadcopters to strike patrolling military vehicles. That attack resulted in the deaths of Major Omer Minhas Nasir and Havildar Muhammad Adnan Khan, alongside the neutralization of eight terrorists.

Pakistan has experienced a steady increase in security challenges, particularly in Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, since the Afghan Taliban took control in 2021. According to a Centre for Research and Security Studies (CRSS) report from the second quarter of 2026, these two provinces constituted nearly 96% of all violence-related fatalities nationwide, with Balochistan recording 265 deaths and 94 separate violent incidents.

stories.title: FIFA Confirms Diallo and Tashima as Challengers to Gianni Infantino
stories.summary:
FIFA has officially confirmed that French football chief Philippe Diallo and veteran Japanese official Kozo Tashima will run against incumbent Gianni Infantino in the upcoming presidential election next March. Infantino has faced criticism from various quarters, notably regarding an aborted plan to introduce private investment into the World Cup. However, the Swiss leader continues to hold substantial backing from multiple confederations ahead of the vote.

Philippe Diallo, who leads the French Football Federation, represents UEFA, the European governing body that has voiced the strongest opposition to Infantino. Kozo Tashima is a former head of the Japan Football Association and a current member of the FIFA Council. Ramon Vega, a former Swiss Tottenham defender who previously expressed interest in challenging Infantino, was excluded from the final candidate list. FIFA's electoral committee will examine the confirmed candidacies before making a final admission decision.

In response to the upcoming election, Diallo expressed interest in meeting with Tashima to potentially join forces and unseat Infantino. Tashima acknowledged the necessity of discussions with the French official but emphasized the need to carefully evaluate whether sharing similar programs is enough to unite, or if a more tactical strategy is required to defeat the current president. Notably, Tashima's candidacy runs counter to the Asian Football Confederation, which announced its official support for Infantino's re-election.

This election challenge is significant for the future governance of global football. While Infantino retains strong support from the Confederation of African Football and CONMEBOL in South America—bolstered by skyrocketing FIFA profits and increased distributions to member federations—the opposition highlights deep divisions within international football leadership over financial strategies and administration under Infantino's tenure.

stories.title: South Africa Defeats Bangladesh by Nine Wickets to Claim Top WTC Spot
stories.summary:
South Africa secured a dominant nine-wicket victory over Bangladesh on the final day of the first Test at the Wanderers Stadium in Johannesburg. Off-spinner Simon Harmer dismantled the Bangladesh batting order by taking six wickets for 51 runs, leaving the visitors all out for 168. South Africa easily chased down the target of 12 runs, despite losing Marques Ackerman for a duck to Mehidy Hasan.

The victory propelled South Africa to the summit of the World Test Championship table, registering their sixth win out of eight matches in the current cycle. The triumph also marked captain Temba Bavuma's 14th win in 16 Tests, setting a historic record for Test match captains. However, the celebrations were tempered by the announcement that Bavuma will miss the second Test of the series due to a right calf injury sustained while batting.

Bavuma initially retired hurt on the third day with a right calf strain and did not field during Bangladesh's second innings, though he managed to resume batting later in the match. The South African skipper acknowledged the rising expectations and internal pressure facing the team as they prepare for a demanding schedule that includes the remaining Bangladesh Test, three home matches against England, and two away Tests in Sri Lanka.

For Bangladesh, captain Najmul Hossain Shanto highlighted the positive milestone of scoring 400 runs in the first innings on a typically bowler-friendly pitch, signaling team progress. However, Shanto noted that playing the world's best team leaves no room for errors, citing costly missed catches and numerous no-balls as decisive factors that ultimately cost them the match.

stories.title: Ten Killed in Ormara Collision Involving Passenger Coach and LPG Bowser
stories.summary:
At least 10 people, including a woman and a child, lost their lives and several others sustained burn injuries in a severe collision on Thursday. The accident occurred near Basol in Ormara along the Makran coastal highway when a Karachi-bound passenger coach collided with a liquefied petroleum gas bowser. Superintendent of Police for the Makran coastal highway police, Muhammad Aslam Bangulzai, confirmed the death toll.

According to police, the passenger vehicle was travelling from Turbat to Karachi when the impact took place. The collision immediately triggered a fire that engulfed both vehicles, trapping passengers inside before emergency responders could intervene. Rescue teams, coastal highway personnel, and local administration officials were dispatched to the site, and the injured victims were transferred to the Ormara Health Centre for medical treatment.

The accident caused major disruptions, leaving traffic on the Makran coastal highway suspended for several hours. Long queues of stranded vehicles formed near Basol and Ormara as a result of the blockage. This tragedy follows a series of fatal accidents on the same coastal highway in recent months, including an August crash that killed six family members, a March collision that claimed seven lives, and a January vehicle overturn that killed 10 people and injured over 30 others.

stories.title: COP31 Negotiators Release Revised Draft Deal Omitting Fossil Fuel References
stories.summary:
Climate negotiators at the COP31 summit in Antalya, Turkiye, published a slimmed-down draft deal on Thursday that completely removes any reference to ending the use of fossil fuels. The conference, facing an impending Friday deadline, is unfolding as global policymakers grapple with competing crises including war and soaring living costs, even as extreme weather events like droughts, heatwaves, and floods intensify worldwide. The revised text is significantly weaker than the initial draft released on Monday, stripping out targets for fossil fuel phaseouts, electrification, and a $120 billion adaptation finance goal for developing nations.

The removal of key provisions drew sharp criticism from observers and advocacy groups. Mohamed Adow, director of the think tank Power Shift Africa, warned that the current version risks rendering the summit a "ghost COP" with no tangible achievements. Despite the omissions, Thursday's draft retains an acknowledgment that global warming could surpass the critical 1.5 degrees Celsius threshold. It also calls for sustained, rapid greenhouse gas emissions cuts and encourages the deployment of carbon removal technologies, a provision critics argue may provide loopholes for the fossil fuel industry to continue polluting.

Australia, co-leading negotiations alongside Turkiye under a split presidency, maintained that the opening draft was always structured as a broad document intended to be narrowed. Historically, consensus among the nearly 200 participating nations frequently pushes proceedings past the official Friday closing schedule by more than 24 hours. Fundamental disagreements persist regarding financial responsibilities, mitigation strategies, and the required pace of climate action.

The updated document includes a non-binding call for global cooperation to elevate electricity's share of world energy consumption from roughly 23 percent to 35 percent by 2035. This goal, originally championed by host nation Turkiye and backed by approximately 75 countries, previously faced resistance from developing nations over funding concerns. Jasper Inventor, head of the Greenpeace COP31 delegation, argued that the electrification target lacks clarity on accelerating the fossil fuel transition and criticized carbon removal inclusions as a profound backward step for global climate efforts.

stories.title: Xi, Trump, and Putin Hold First Trilateral Summit at APEC in China
stories.summary:
The leaders of China, the United States, and Russia commenced their first trilateral meeting on Thursday on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, China. Chinese President Xi Jinping, US President Donald Trump, and Russian President Vladimir Putin gathered at Kylin Villa for talks. While Beijing described the objective as safeguarding world peace, critics and analysts expressed concern that the high-level meeting is primarily symbolic and could signal an effort by major powers to carve out global spheres of influence.

The summit coincides with ongoing geopolitical conflicts, including Russia's military offensive in Ukraine nearing its fifth year, and a war involving Iran that has impacted global oil supplies and consumer prices. Before the three-way talks, Trump held his first meeting with Putin since August 2025, followed by a separate bilateral discussion with Xi, marking their third meeting of the year. The leaders' agendas varied across official accounts, with discussions touching on the Ukraine conflict, trade, artificial intelligence guidelines, and nuclear disarmament following the expiration of a bilateral US-Russia arms treaty in February.

The meeting drew sharp criticism from political opponents and analysts who warned that the optics would benefit the domestic standings of Xi and Putin while potentially undermining US interests. Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer accused Putin and Xi of manipulating the US president. Meanwhile, the summit featured notable diplomatic exchanges, including Xi greeting Trump with an airport reception involving an air-force flyover, a gesture reciprocating Trump's welcome in the US last September.

The APEC gathering also brought together other regional leaders, such as Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, South Korean President Lee Jae Myung, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, and Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese. Despite underlying regional tensions, the leaders participated in traditional events, including the APEC family photo wearing special scarves. Xi opened the main summit proceedings by urging participating nations to lower barriers to trade and investment.

stories.title: Pakistan Navy Enhances Combat Capabilities Across All Operational Domains
stories.summary:
Chief of the Naval Staff Admiral Naveed Ashraf announced that the Pakistan Navy has significantly improved its combat readiness across all operational domains. Speaking at the graduation parade of the Pakistan Air Force Academy Asghar Khan in Risalpur, located in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Nowshera district, Admiral Ashraf emphasized that the navy is steadily modernizing its fleet.

Key advancements highlighted by the naval chief include the introduction of state-of-the-art warships, Hangor-class submarines, indigenously developed long-range weapons, unmanned systems, and the creation of the Pakistan Maritime Science & Technology Park. He noted that contemporary warfare is driven by rapid technological advancements and expanding into electronic warfare, cyber, space, cognitive fields, artificial intelligence, and autonomous systems.

Addressing the regional security climate, Admiral Ashraf pointed out that geopolitical dynamics have grown more complex due to tensions in the Middle East. He noted that the ongoing Operation Muhafizul Bahr, launched in March following the Middle East conflict, continues successfully. He also reflected on the May 2025 Pakistan-India conflict, known as Marka-i-Haq, stating that the armed forces proved invincible and capable of deterring aggression, with the navy successfully keeping the Indian Navy at bay.

Turkey’s air force chief, General Rafet Dalkiran, attended the parade as a guest. Admiral Ashraf praised the enduring friendship between Pakistan and Turkey, and reaffirmed that while Pakistan remains a peace-abiding nation dedicated to regional stability and diplomacy, its armed forces are fully prepared to defend the country against any threat.

stories.title: IEA Warns Middle East Crisis Poses Historic Threat to Energy Security
stories.summary:
The ongoing Middle East crisis, triggered in February by US and Israeli bombings of Iran, represents the largest threat to energy security in history, according to the International Energy Agency (IEA). In its flagship annual World Energy Outlook released in Paris, the agency warned that the disruption has far surpassed the scale of the oil shocks seen in the 1970s, leaving consumers to shoulder the burden of soaring prices and supply shortages.

Energy exports from the Gulf region have faced severe obstacles as Iran enforces a blockade of the Strait of Hormuz and targets nearby oil tankers. Despite American efforts to escort commercial vessels through the crucial channel—which previously handled roughly one-fifth of global oil shipments—supply chains remain heavily interrupted. IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol noted in the report that governments have tried to shield households by boosting supplies and utilizing alternative routes, but consumers continue to face higher costs and reduced availability.

Released concurrently with the COP31 climate talks in Turkey, the report incorporates scenarios evaluating how long-term disruption might alter global energy markets. In its standard middle scenario, the IEA projects that global oil demand will peak around 2030 before slowly declining, while gas demand is expected to grow until approximately 2035. However, additional scenarios factoring in a prolonged Middle East conflict indicate deep, lasting impacts.

Birol emphasized that as traditional buffers diminish, the global economy and energy sector are forced to absorb the shocks directly. He added that there is no foreseeable path for the global energy landscape to revert to its pre-crisis state.

stories.title: COMSATS University Offers Free Education for Industrial and Mine Workers' Children
stories.summary:
COMSATS University Islamabad (CUI) has announced 100 percent free education opportunities for eligible industrial and mine workers alongside their children under the Punjab Workers Welfare Fund (PWWF) Talent Scholarship Programme. The initiative applies to admissions for the Spring 2027 semester across multiple campuses, including Islamabad, Lahore, Abbottabad, Wah, Sahiwal, Vehari, and Attock.

Under this scholarship scheme, successful applicants receive fully funded education that covers their tuition fees, hostel accommodations, and daily transportation costs. The scholarship remains active for the normal duration of the chosen degree programme. However, students who are required to repeat a course or an entire semester must pay the standard dues outlined by university regulations.

To qualify for the PWWF scholarship, workers must meet specific criteria under the Industrial Relations Act of 2010, hold a valid Social Security Card, and possess a minimum of three years of work experience in a factory registered under the Factories Act of 1934 or a mine registered under the Mines Act of 1923. Additionally, employers must satisfy legal requirements under the Workers’ Welfare Fund Ordinance of 1971 or the Companies’ Profits (Workers’ Participation) Act of 1968. Children of deceased or disabled workers registered with EOBI or Social Security are also eligible if they meet family welfare conditions.

Prospective students must apply for the scholarship simultaneously while submitting their online admission applications to a single-degree programme. Applicants are required to deliver the necessary hard-copy documents directly to the admission office of their chosen campus before the respective deadline.

stories.title: Asif Zardari and Bilawal Bhutto to Discuss New Provinces and Constitutional Amendments
stories.summary:
Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari is scheduled to travel from Karachi to Islamabad to hold a high-level meeting with President Asif Ali Zardari. The discussions between the father and son will center on the country's current political landscape and internal party affairs.

According to sources, the agenda includes proposals regarding the creation of new administrative units and provinces, potential constitutional amendments, and the possibility of a national referendum. The talks come at a critical juncture as the PPP leadership weighs its official stance on various constitutional and political issues, alongside anticipated shifts in political alignments.

Another key item slated for discussion is the potential convening of a meeting of the PPP's Central Executive Committee (CEC). This proposed gathering would serve as a broader forum for party leaders to evaluate the prevailing political environment and formulate future strategic initiatives.

Political observers are closely monitoring the outcome of the meeting between President Zardari and Bilawal Bhutto Zardari. The decisions made during their discussions are expected to significantly influence the party's upcoming policy directions regarding regional governance and legislative reforms.

stories.title: inDrive Conducts Nationwide Safety Workshops and Training Across Pakistan
stories.summary:
Ride-hailing platform inDrive organizes regular nationwide safety workshops across Pakistan to cultivate road etiquette, personal accountability, and continuous learning among its drivers. The comprehensive curriculum goes beyond basic transit logistics to cover foundational road safety, including adherence to traffic laws, speed limits, pre-trip vehicle inspections, and defensive driving techniques suited for adverse weather conditions.

In addition to driving rules, the sessions focus on professional conduct, boundary management, and de-escalation strategies for handling aggressive, unpredictable, or intoxicated passengers. A dedicated passenger safety module instructs participants on maintaining professional etiquette, identifying safe boarding and drop-off zones, following agreed routes, and assisting elderly, disabled, or vulnerable commuters, alongside guidelines for handling roadside breakdowns, accidents, or security incidents.

The training also provides an in-depth walkthrough of inDrive's digital safety architecture. Drivers learn to use pre-ride tools displaying passenger ratings and exact destinations, privacy-protecting in-app calls and chats, and AI-powered moderation filters that ban non-compliant accounts. Active in-trip safeguards are covered, such as proactive trip monitoring for prolonged stops, encrypted in-app audio recording for conflict deterrence, emergency SOS integration for instant police or ambulance access, and designated trusted contacts for critical situations.

Furthermore, the program reviews financial security by highlighting inDrive's comprehensive accident and health insurance coverage in Pakistan, provided in partnership with Waada and renewed annually. This policy protects active rides by covering accidental death, total disability, immediate medical expenses, and hospital cash benefits. Through these behavioral workshops, digital guardrails, and financial protections, inDrive aims to empower drivers and protect commuters across the country.

stories.title: Chinese President Xi Calls for Complete Elimination of Nuclear Weapons
stories.summary:
Chinese President Xi Jinping has advocated for the comprehensive prohibition and complete destruction of nuclear weapons during a meeting with US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin. Speaking on Thursday, Xi emphasized that the ultimate objective is to build a world entirely free of nuclear arms.

According to China’s official Xinhua news agency, the Chinese leader stated that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought under any circumstances. He stressed that every possible effort must be directed toward preventing such a conflict from occurring.

The high-level meeting brought together the leaders of three major nuclear powers to discuss global security matters. Xi's remarks underscored Beijing's official stance on disarmament and the avoidance of atomic warfare.

The discussions highlight ongoing international dialogues regarding strategic stability and the reduction of nuclear arsenals. No further details regarding additional agreements from the gathering were provided.

stories.title: Nicholls and Phillips Lead New Zealand Fightback in First India Test
stories.summary:
New Zealand reached 243-5 at stumps on the opening day of the first Test against India in Wellington, recovering from a precarious 70-5 after lunch. Henry Nicholls scored an unbeaten 113, while Glenn Phillips finished the day not out on 94, rescuing the hosts with an unbroken 173-run partnership.

India captain Shubman Gill won the toss and elected to bowl on a testing Basin Reserve pitch with ample grass, prompting India's fast bowlers to utilize fuller deliveries aimed at the stumps. Fast bowler Jasprit Bumrah made a brilliant return to Test cricket after nearly a year away, taking 3-52 from 17 overs. Bumrah dismissed captain Tom Latham with the third ball of the innings, later adding Daryl Mitchell and Tom Blundell to his tally. New Zealand had slumped to 60-4 at lunch following early wickets by Bumrah, Anshul Kamboj, and Akash Deep.

Nicholls arrived at the crease early in the morning session and played with patience and control to secure his 12th Test hundred and his sixth at the Basin Reserve. He was dropped by Devdutt Padikkal on 102 after mistiming a pull shot off a delivery. Phillips joined Nicholls shortly after lunch and immediately accelerated the scoring with powerful drives and deft cut shots, putting pressure on the visiting bowlers.

Indian batting coach Sitanshu Kotak praised Bumrah's exceptional line, length, and movement on the pitch. Kotak noted that the less experienced bowlers in the squad could learn valuable lessons from Bumrah's adaptability to New Zealand conditions as the series continues.

stories.title: SECP Directs Companies to Transfer Unclaimed Dividends to Government Account
stories.summary:
The Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP) has ordered all listed companies to deposit dividends and profits that have remained unclaimed for three years into a designated federal government account. The directive was issued under a circular dated November 16, utilizing powers conferred by the SECP Act of 1997 and the relevant sections of the Companies Act.
